LESSON: READING 11.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: LESSONS LEARNT

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.4: Reading 11.4.1 Intensive Reading: Lessons Learnt

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 11.4.1 Intensive Reading: Lessons Learnt. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What issues in the society are addressed by stories?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the lessons learnt in a short story
2. appreciate the role of stories in addressing societal issues

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 11.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: LESSONS LEARNT
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 11.4.1 Intensive Reading: Lessons Learnt helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 11.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: LESSONS LEARNT
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the lessons learnt in a short story

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the lessons learnt in a short story. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the lessons learnt in a short story.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 11.4.1 Intensive Reading: Lessons Learnt”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the lessons learnt in a short story. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the role of stories in addressing societal issues

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of stories in addressing societal issues. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of stories in addressing societal issues.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 11.4.1 Intensive Reading: Lessons Learnt to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of stories in addressing societal issues. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 11.4.1 Intensive Reading: Lessons Learnt is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 11.4.1 Intensive Reading: Lessons Learnt”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the lessons learnt in a short story)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 11.4.1 Intensive Reading: Lessons Learnt to a partner. (skill: appreciate the role of stories in addressing societal issues)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 11.4.1 Intensive Reading: Lessons Learnt to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the lessons learnt in a short story.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of stories in addressing societal issues.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 11.4.1 Intensive Reading: Lessons Learnt from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 11.4.1 Intensive Reading: Lessons Learnt: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Reading 11.4.1 Intensive Reading: Lessons Learnt?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What issues in the society are addressed by stories?
2. How can one derive lessons from a short story?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 11.4.1 Intensive Reading: Lessons Learnt means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the lessons learnt in a short story.
5. Be able to: appreciate the role of stories in addressing societal issues.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
